item.title: Senate passes bill to reform senior secondary education
item.description: By Henry Umoru The Senate has passed the National Senior Secondary Education Commission (Amendment) Bill, 2026, seeking to strengthen the administration, coordination and governance of public senior secondary education in Nigeria. The executive bill, sponsored by President Bola Tinubu, was transmitted to the Senate in July 2026 for legislative consideration. The proposed legislation, titled the National Senior Secondary Education Commission Act (Amendment) Bill, 2026 (SB. 1075), was passed on Wednesday after consideration of the report of the Senate Committee on Education (Basic and Secondary). Senator Orji Uzor Kalu (APC, Abia North) presented the committee’s report on behalf of its chairman, Senator Lawal Adamu Usman (Kaduna Central). Following a clause-by-clause consideration of the report at the Committee of the Whole, the Senate approved the bill, which was subsequently read for the third time and passed. Presenting the report, Kalu urged the Senate to consider and adopt the recommendations of the committee on the proposed legislation. According to the report, the National Senior Secondary Education Commission was established under the National Senior Secondary Education Commission Act, 2023, to regulate and promote the development of senior secondary education in Nigeria. It stated that experience gained in implementing the Act had revealed areas requiring amendments to strengthen governance, improve coordination between the Federal and State Governments, promote accountability and support the effective implementation of national education policies. The report added that the proposed amendments were intended to address the identified challenges and make the legislation more effective in achieving its objectives. Kalu disclosed that the House of Representatives had also considered the bill and referred it to its Committee on Basic Education and Services for further legislative action. He said this informed the decision to conduct a joint stakeholder hearing and clause-by-clause consideration to ensure comprehensive consolidation, a uniform report and smoother legislative proceedings. Recall that President Tinubu transmitted the executive bill to the Senate in July through a letter read by Senate President Godswill Akpabio during plenary. In the letter, Tinubu said the Federal Executive Council had approved the amendment bill at its meeting on April 30, 2026, before the Federal Ministry of Justice vetted and finalised it in line with constitutional provisions and legislative drafting standards. The President said the proposed amendment was part of his administration’s commitment to strengthening educational institutions in the national interest. Following the presentation of the bill, Akpabio referred it to the Senate Committee on Rules and Business for legislative processing and directed it to report back within one week. item.title: 2027: Only Yari, Alake, Idris can speak for Tinubu campaign, APC-PCC declares
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC has restricted the right to speak on its behalf to three persons, ordering that everyone previously announced in that role be dissolved into the Directorate of Media and Strategic Communications as members. The Chief of Staff to the President and Deputy Director-General (Administration) of the Council, Femi Gbajabiamila, announced the changes in a statement issued on Wednesday, titled “Reorganization of Media and Communications Structure”. According to the statement, “The Council has approved that only the campaign’s Director General, Senator Abdulaziz Yari; the Minister of Solid Minerals, Dele Alake, as official Spokesperson; and the Minister of Information and National Orientation, Alhaji Mohammed Idris, will speak on behalf of the Council.” Gbajabiamila said the Council made the changes “to ensure more cohesive, disciplined, and effective public engagement”. He said that “all previously announced persons in this capacity shall henceforth dissolve into the Directorate of Media and Strategic Communications as members.” The statement also put broadcasters on notice. Radio and television stations were advised “to take note of these changes and act accordingly”. On appearances by other persons, the statement said: “The campaign will delegate appropriate person(s) for appearances where and when necessary.” The post 2027: Only Yari, Alake, Idris can speak for Tinubu campaign, APC-PCC declares appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Obi is desperate, not wired for long-term solutions — Oshiomhole
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Senator Adams Oshiomhole has accused Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate Peter Obi of focusing on importation rather than job creation and long-term solutions, alleging that his promise to serve only four years reflects desperation to become president. Oshiomhole made the remarks while campaigning for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Akure, the Ondo State capital, on Wednesday. Framing the 2027 election as a choice about Nigeria’s future, he urged young voters to back Tinubu and contrasted what he described as the President’s long-term development agenda and plans to improve the power sector with Obi’s business record and four-year pledge. Addressing young Nigerians, the APC chieftain urged students, graduates and young workers to compare the time it takes industrialists such as Aliko Dangote to establish factories and create jobs with what he described as Obi’s focus on setting up shopping malls. “That said, I need to talk to us, you young people. What this election is about is you. You as students, some of you are graduates, some of you are young workers. You talk to Dangote and ask him how long does it take him to set up a factory, to set up a refinery that today employs 10s of 1000s of workers. Then go and ask Obi how long it takes him to set up a shopping mall. To set up a shopping mall, you need short-term funds, and that is the logic of Peter Obi,” he said. Oshiomhole alleged that Obi was not inclined to develop long-term solutions that could produce sustainable growth. He also questioned Obi’s business record, asking why an unemployed person should accept advice on job creation from someone he accused of selling imported products instead of locally made Yoruba Adire. “He cannot; he’s not wired to think of long-term solutions that produce sustainable growth and development. Another one: if there is anybody who is unemployed, ask Obi, why are you selling imported products?” Oshiomhole asked. He further argued that a person whose main business was importation could not credibly lecture Nigerians on job creation, and described Obi’s pledge to serve for four years as evidence of what he called desperation. “So, anyone whose main business is importation cannot lecture us about job creation because he doesn’t mean it. And for you to see the desperation, he will say he will do four years. So he is a man who just wants it to be said that once upon a time there was a Peter in the villa. Nigeria needs statesmen, not petty traders in politics,” he added. Turning to Tinubu’s re-election bid, Oshiomhole said the President knew the need to increase the purchasing power of poorer Nigerians and create jobs. item.title: Tinubu awards N100m FG Savings Bond to each victorious Flamingos player
item.description: –Coach receives ₦100m; technical crew members get ₦50m each By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu on Wednesday announced the award of a ₦100 million Federal Government Savings Bond to each player on Nigeria’s victorious U-17 women’s football team, the Flamingos. The bonds attract an annual interest rate of 14 per cent. The investment by the government for the players is for five years. President Tinubu also announced a cash gift of ₦100 million for the coach and ₦50 million for each member of the technical crew. The President announced the rewards during a reception at the Presidential Villa in Abuja for the Flamingos, who reportedly won the U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The Flamingos defeated Japan to become the first African team to win the tournament. President Tinubu was represented at the reception by the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu. item.title: Video: First lady receives Flamingos in Aso Villa
item.description: Nigeria’s First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, on Wednesday hosted the Flamingos at the Presidential Villa in Abuja following their historic victory at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Mrs Tinubu welcomed the players on behalf of President Bola Tinubu, alongside the wife of the vice-president, Nana Shettima, and other government officials. First Lady Remi Tinubu receives Nigeria's Flamingos at the Presidential Villa on behalf of President Tinubu after their historic U-17 World Cup triumph. Video Credit : NTA News pic.twitter.com/PQUYCSZMYr — Vanguard Newspapers (@vanguardngrnews) November 11, 2026 At the reception, the First Lady presented flowers to members of the team in recognition of their achievement. The Flamingos made history on Saturday by defeating Japan 2-1 in the final, becoming the first African country to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Awawu Bashiru gave Nigeria the lead in the 39th minute, while Oluebube Umejiaku extended the advantage shortly after the second half began. Japan pulled one back through Fuki Ito in the 80th minute, but Nigeria held on to secure the title. President Tinubu had earlier congratulated the team, describing their victory as a landmark achievement for Nigeria and women’s football in Africa. item.title: Diezani’s suit ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍​⁠⁠‌‌​‍‌​seeking to reclaim forfeited assets stalled
item.description: A suit filed by the former Minister of Petroleum, Mrs Diezani Alison-Madueke, seeking to reclaim all her forfeited assets to the Federal Government on Wednesday suffered a setback at the Federal High Court in Abuja. The suit, which was fixed for mention before Justice Inyang Ekwo, could not go on shortly after the case was called. Diezani’s lawyer, Eko-Ejembi Eko, SAN, after he announced his appearance, prayed the court for an adjournment on the ground that he was just coming into the matter for the first time and that he would need more time to study the file. The EFCC’s counsel, Paul Mgbeoma, did not oppose the application, and with the agreement of the parties, Justice Ekwo adjourned the matter until Jan. 26, for further mention. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the ex-minister, in the suit, is praying the court to order the EFCC to retrieve from persons, either natural or corporate, to whom it had sold off her seized assets or property. Diezani, in an amended suit, sought an order setting aside the commission’s public notice issued, upon which it conducted the public sale by auction. The anti-graft agency had, in the public notice, announced the sale of the former minister’s assets beginning from Jan. 9, 2023, to Jan. 13, 2023. Against the announcement, the ex-minister had, in the originating motion marked FHC/ABJ/CS/21/2023, sued the EFCC as the sole respondent. In the suit dated and filed on Jan. 6, 2023, she sought an order extending the time to seek leave to apply to the court for an order to set aside the EFCC’s public notice issued to conduct a public sale on her property, among others. NAN reports that on July 1, Justice Ekwo granted the application filed by the ex-minister to present evidence of the London court that acquitted her. But the EFCC opposed the application filed by Diezani to present the evidence of her acquittal by the Southwark Crown Court, London, in the UK. The EFCC, in a further counter-affidavit to Diezani’s request, prayed Justice Ekwo to dismiss the application. The commission argued that the purported acquittal of Diezani by a foreign criminal court in charges preferred against her was not material or relevant to the specific issues for determination before the instant court. (NAN) The post Diezani’s suit ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍​⁠⁠‌‌​‍‌​seeking to reclaim forfeited assets stalled appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nasarawa 2027: Nobody can intimidate us, SDP’s Adamu tells supporters
item.description: The governorship candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) in Nasarawa State, Adamu Abdullahi, has vowed that his supporters will resist any attempt to intimidate them ahead of the 2027 governorship election. Adamu, a former Inspector-General of Police, alleged that some political actors were boasting about having an anointed candidate who would emerge governor regardless of the people’s choice, describing such claims as an indication of plans to manipulate the election. He spoke in Hausa while addressing supporters during a political gathering in Doma Local Government Area of the state on Monday. “Nobody can intimidate us. Nobody can scare us with the claim that they have an anointed candidate who must become governor, whether we like it or not,” he said. Adamu argued that insisting on the emergence of a preferred candidate irrespective of the outcome of the election amounted to a threat to the democratic process. “What that means, in essence, is that they want to rig the election. We will not allow that, and we will not accept it,” he added. The SDP candidate urged his supporters to remain at their polling units after voting to ensure that their ballots were counted and the results properly recorded. He warned that leaving polling stations immediately after voting could create room for electoral manipulation. “Do not cast your vote and go home, because doing so could give them the opportunity to compromise and manipulate the election results,” he said. Adamu also claimed that the SDP was gaining more support in the state, alleging that members of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), including women, were leaving the party to join his political movement. “Every day, their supporters keep leaving their party (APC) to join us in the SDP because the people have realised that they have nothing to offer the masses,” he said. He assured the women who attended the gathering that his political movement would work with them to address issues affecting ordinary residents. “By Allah’s grace, we will work together to deliver all the things we are supposed to do for the masses,” he added. Describing the turnout in Doma as evidence of his growing support, Adamu said the people of the area were united behind his political ambition and urged them to remain committed to the movement. item.title: VIDEO: Tinubu Receives Flamingos In Abuja After World Cup Victory
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has received the Flamingos after winning Africa’s first-ever U-17 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, received the victorious players and technical crew on behalf of the President at the Presidential Banquet Hall, Abuja. ﻿ The U-17 team won their first FIFA World Cup title after defeating Japan 2-1 in the final on November 7, with goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku securing the historic victory. The Flamingos lost their opener 2-1 to Poland, but dominated in the remaining matches, defeating defending champions North Korea, Puerto Rico, and Mexico. Their first-ever appearance in the final was sealed with a 3-1 victory over Brazil, before taking home the trophy after beating Japan. Flamingos celebrating their U-17 FIFA Women’s World Cup The players have received commendations from government officials and football fans around the world. President Tinubu congratulated the Flamingos for becoming the first African team to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Tinubu, in a statement by his spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, said he received the news upon his return from campaign engagements in Akwa Ibom and Rivers States. He also described Nigeria’s maiden triumph as a proud moment for the country and a landmark achievement for African women’s football. The Senate also pledged a ₦100 million reward for the Flamingos. The pledge followed a motion moved by the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Sports, Senator Abdul Ningi, who congratulated the players on their outstanding performance and commended the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) for its role in the team’s achievement. The latest feat by a Nigerian sports team came less than two years after the senior women’s football team, Super Falcons, won their 10th Women’s Africa Cup of Nations title in Morocco. item.title: Jonathan to present Buhari’s biography; Tinubu, others to grace unveiling
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja Former President Goodluck Jonathan will be the chief presenter of “Muhammadu Buhari: The Authorised Biography” at a public presentation in Abuja on Thursday, 19 November 2026, with President Bola Tinubu expected as guest of honour. Chairman of the Planning Committee, Engr Suleiman Adamu, a former minister of water resources, disclosed this on Wednesday at a press conference. According to him, the event will be chaired by former Niger Republic President Mahamadou Issoufou. The three volumes carry Forewords by Issoufou, General Yakubu Gowon and General Abdulsalami Abubakar. Adamu said the occasion was designed to be more than a political gathering. “We are deliberately seeking to make the occasion broader than a gathering of political associates. Muhammadu Buhari was a partisan political actor during important periods of his life, but his biography belongs to the historical record of Nigeria. “For that reason, we hope the presentation will draw participation from across political, regional, professional and institutional lines,” he said. Adamu added that the programme would bring together “family, associates, colleagues, former officials, members of the political class, the military community, academia, the diplomatic community, the private sector, civil society, the media and the wider reading public.” The biography was authorised by Buhari during his lifetime and developed with his extensive personal participation through sustained interviews and other research engagements. It also draws on several years of documentary research and interviews with people who knew, worked with, opposed or advised him. The first volume, “Buhari: The Phenomenon”, traces his origins, military career, years as military head of state and long journey through opposition politics to the 2015 presidential victory. The second, “Buhari: The Presidency”, examines the eight years between 2015 and 2023. The third, “Buhari: The Reckoning”, considers the record on the economy, security, infrastructure, foreign affairs, anti-corruption, institutional reform and social policy. Adamu said the books must travel beyond the ceremony. “We regard it as important that universities, libraries, research institutions, military and security institutions, public agencies, diplomatic missions and other repositories of national memory acquire the volumes and make them available to students, researchers and future generations. We invite Nigerians to approach these volumes with curiosity rather than with predetermined conclusions,” he said. item.title: Ooni, Olubadan, six other monarchs hold strategic meeting in Ibadan
item.description: …deliberate on security, regional development, 2027 elections By Adeola Badru Prominent traditional rulers from across the South-West on Tuesday converged on Ibadan, the Oyo State capital, for a closed-door meeting to deliberate on critical issues affecting the region. The meeting, held at the palace of the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, has in attendance the Ooni of Ife, Oba Enitan Ogunwusi; the Olubadan, Oba Rashidi Ladoja; the Deji of Akure, Oba Aladetoyinbo Aladelusi; and the Elegushi of the Ikate-Elegushi Kingdom, Oba Saheed Ademola. Other monarchs attending the meeting include the Ewi of Ado-Ekiti, the Alake of Egbaland, the Ayangburen of Ikorodu, the Aseyin of Iseyin and the Alago of Ago-Iwoye, among other prominent traditional rulers. A credible palace source confided in Vanguard that the monarchs would deliberate on a range of issues concerning the security, economic development and political future of the South-West. According to the source, discussions would also extend to preparations for the 2027 general elections, alongside other matters of regional importance. The source said, “The traditional rulers would deliberate on the various issues affecting the region. “Some of the issues pencilled down for discussion include security, economic development and the 2027 general elections, among others.” The post Ooni, Olubadan, six other monarchs hold strategic meeting in Ibadan appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: AFCON 2027Q: Full house in Uyo as Super Eagles set for Tanzania clash
item.description: The Super Eagles have recorded a full house in camp in Uyo as preparations intensify for Friday’s 2026 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying clash against Tanzania. The Nigerian team is stepping up preparations for the encounter, scheduled for November 13 at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo, Akwa Ibom State. All 24 invited players are now in camp, with the coaching crew preparing for the team’s second training session ahead of the fixture. Among the players in camp are Calvin Bassey, Ola Aina, Alex Iwobi, Wilfred Ndidi, Ademola Lookman, Moses Simon, Taiwo Awoniyi and Akor Adams. Others include Arthur Okonkwo, Semi Ajayi, Benjamin Fredericks, Alhassan Yusuf, Bright Osayi-Samuel, Tochukwu Nnadi, Chibuike Nwaiwu, Tolu Arokodare and Francis Uzoho. Stanley Nwabali, Tijani Samson, Suleiman Mubarak, Abdullahi Bewene, Moses Usor, Bruno Onyemaechi and Fisayo Dele-Bashiru complete the list of players in camp. The encounter against Tanzania will be an important test for the Super Eagles as they continue their preparations for the continental assignment. The team will be hoping to make the most of home advantage when both sides meet in Uyo on Friday. item.title: FG moves against food fraud, targets practices linked to 53,000 deaths
item.description: By Chioma Obinna The Federal Government has unveiled a multi-pronged strategy to tackle food contamination, adulteration and unsafe processing practices blamed for an estimated 50 million food-borne illnesses and 53,000 related deaths in Nigeria. The government also warned that individuals and businesses involved in the production and sale of contaminated or adulterated food risk between six months and two years’ imprisonment upon conviction. The Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Dr Kingsley Tochukwu Udeh, disclosed this in Abuja on Tuesday, saying the government would strengthen enforcement of food safety laws and collaborate with the Ministry of Justice and the Attorney-General to prosecute offenders. Udeh said the measures were aimed at protecting Nigerians from the growing dangers associated with unsafe food and ensuring that those responsible for food-related violations were held accountable. He described the scale of food-borne diseases as alarming, citing a World Health Organisation (WHO) report released in June, which estimated that 866 million people worldwide suffered food-borne illnesses in 2021, resulting in 1.52 million deaths, including 143,000 children under five. The report also put the global economic burden of food-borne diseases at $310 billion. According to the minister, WHO studies have established that unsafe food can cause more than 200 diseases, ranging from diarrhoea to cancer. He recalled the deaths of five members of a family in Kogi State in August 2026 after consuming fufu processed from cassava flour, as well as 49 fatalities in Ondo State in September following the consumption of locally prepared alcoholic and herbal drinks contaminated with methanol. Udeh said the incidents underscored the urgent need for stronger food safety regulations, effective monitoring and public awareness to prevent further loss of lives. He commended the Registrar of the Nigerian Council of Food Science and Technology (NiCFoST), Mrs Veronica Ezeh, for her efforts to rid the country of unwholesome and adulterated food products. Earlier, Ezeh raised concerns over dangerous food processing and preservation practices, warning that the use of unauthorised chemicals and substances was exposing Nigerians to serious health risks. She identified artificial ripening of fruits with calcium carbide, the application of dichlorvos, popularly known as Sniper, on beans and grains, the use of paracetamol to tenderise meat, and the application of detergents and bleaching agents in cassava processing as some of the harmful practices. She also cited the adulteration of palm oil with prohibited colourants, including Sudan IV dye. According to her, these practices have contributed to increasing cases of liver cirrhosis, kidney diseases, cancer and damage to other vital organs. To address the situation, the registrar outlined measures, including strict enforcement of Sections 243 to 245 of the Criminal Code Act, Cap C38, Laws of the Federation 2004

item.title: Setback for C’River NDC as Deputy Governorship candidate quits, backs Otu
item.description: …governorship candidate expresses shock By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, in Cross River State has suffered a setback ahead of the 2027 governorship election, following the withdrawal of its Deputy Governorship candidate, Mrs. Stella Charles Archibong, from the party’s ticket. Archibong announced her exit in a statement made available to newsmen in Calabar on Wednesday, declaring support for Governor Bassey Otu’s re-election bid under the Back to South Movement. She said her decision followed extensive consultations with elders, family members, the Christian community and political stakeholders across the state. According to her, her responsibility to Cross River was greater than her personal political ambition, hence her resolve to align with the political direction of the Otu administration. “My responsibility to Cross River State is bigger than my individual ambition,” she declared. Archibong also expressed appreciation to the NDC State Chairman, Mr. Goddy Akpama, the party’s governorship candidate, Mr. John Odey, and the national leadership for the opportunity to serve on the party’s platform. She apologised to supporters who might feel disappointed by her decision, and thanked them for their support and confidence throughout her political engagement. Reacting, Odey described her withdrawal as surprising, but urged party members and supporters to remain calm and demonstrate maturity. In a statement, he said the development required calmness, mutual respect and responsible leadership. “This development has come as a surprise. I believe that moments such as this call for calm, maturity, mutual respect, and responsible leadership,” he said. Odey said he held Archibong in high regard and respected her contributions and commitment to the aspirations of Cross River. He disclosed that consultations were ongoing with party leaders, stakeholders and concerned individuals to understand the circumstances surrounding her withdrawal and determine the appropriate next steps. The NDC candidate, however, assured supporters that the party remained committed to building a prosperous, inclusive and economically productive state. item.title: Buhari wanted full military onslaught against N’Delta Avengers, biography reveals
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Late President Muhammadu Buhari’s instinct, when the Niger Delta Avengers began to press the state through sabotage and threat, was to bring “the weight of the armed forces against the insurgents”, an excerpt from his authorised biography has revealed. The account, credited to former Minister of State, Petroleum, Dr Ibe Kachikwu, is contained in “Muhammadu Buhari: The Authorised Biography”, a three-volume work to be publicly presented on Thursday, 19 November 2026, at the Nigerian Army Conference Centre and Suites, Abuja. Chairman of the Planning Committee and former Minister of Water Resources, Engr. Suleiman Adamu announced the presentation at a press conference on Wednesday in Abuja. According to an excerpt od the biography read at the event, “Buhari’s instinct, Kachikwu recalled, was command.” It states: “He felt as a general, he should watch Nigeria, he owed her, and he wanted to act militarily. But Kachikwu argued that a purely military response would create complications. The federal forces were already stretched, escalation could paralyze the entire industry.” The disagreement reached a head ahead of a meeting with the Pan-Niger Delta Forum. “The president was present, and Kachikwu was present,” the book records. “Buhari was upset at what was unfolding in Niger Delta and was very reluctant to approve dialogue with militants.” The excerpt says that, after persuasion, Buhari accepted engagement, “allowing the peace process to proceed.” The excerpt notes that Buhari “was unwilling to tolerate what he regarded as ransom politics, but was nudged into engagement.” It adds that one of Kachikwu’s favourite photographs of the late President was taken just after that meeting, “when he finally smiled because he had been tense.” Kachikwu teased him afterwards. “See, it’s not so bad after all,” Buhari smiled, he said. The author, Dr Udu Yakubu noted that the late President cooperated with the project but did not control its content. “The work was authorised by President Buhari. That authorisation opened doors,” he said, adding: “The subject has had his voice in the biography, while the biographer has had or retained his independence.” The post Buhari wanted full military onslaught against N’Delta Avengers, biography reveals appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Senate summons NCC, MTN, others over dropped calls, airtime deductions
item.description: By Henry Umoru, Abuja The Senate has summoned the Nigerian Communications Commission, NCC, and telecommunications operators, including MTN, Airtel, Globacom and T2, over persistent dropped calls, failed connections and unexplained airtime deductions suffered by subscribers. The NCC and telecommunication operators are expected to appear before Senator Aliyu Ikra Bilbis, Zamfara Central-led Senate Committee on Communications. The Committee was mandated to invite the Nigerian Communications Commission and telecommunications operators to investigate complaints of airtime deductions for failed calls, dropped calls, prematurely terminated conversations and inflated charges. The committee is also expected to establish the financial losses suffered by subscribers and report back to the Senate within four weeks, with recommendations for further legislative and regulatory action. The resolution of the Senate on Wednesday was a sequel to a motion titled “Need to curb unjustified deductions from subscribers’ airtime resulting from substandard telecommunications services through robust consumer protection.” The motion was sponsored by the Senate Chief Whip, Senator Mohammed Tahir Monguno, APC, Borno North. Senator Ned Nwoko, APC, Delta North, who seconded the motion, described the proposal as a straightforward consumer-protection intervention, insisting that the problem affects virtually every Nigerian who relies on telecommunications services. He lamented the contrast between the quality of telephone services in Nigeria and the seamless connectivity experienced in other countries. Presenting the motion on behalf of Monguno, the Deputy Majority Leader, Senator Lola Ashiru, APC, Kwara South, expressed concerns over consumers being charged for calls that were never successfully completed, with lawmakers demanding accountability, refunds and improved quality of service across the telecommunications industry. According to the Senate, for millions of Nigerians, making a telephone call has increasingly become an expensive gamble, just as poor network connectivity, dropped calls, interrupted conversations and failed connections have become recurring complaints among subscribers, many of whom lose airtime even when calls are not successfully completed. Senators warned that Nigerians should not be made to pay for telecommunications services that have not been effectively delivered. They noted that subscribers are frequently compelled to redial numbers several times before establishing a connection, resulting in additional airtime deductions and financial losses, particularly for low-income earners, traders, students and small business owners. The Senate argued that while network challenges may sometimes be unavoidable, consumers should not bear the financial consequences of service failures beyond their control. item.title: The Promise And The Proof
item.description: Tinubu is asking for time to complete his reforms. His challengers must explain how they would deliver better results. The most consequential promise from today’s campaign platform concerns something Nigerians can judge without a political analyst: whether the lights stay on. Speaking at the APC rally in Dutse, President Bola Tinubu promised reliable electricity, lower living costs, support for smaller businesses and more jobs if re-elected. These commitments reach directly into the daily calculations of households and enterprises. For the tailor buying fuel, the graduate searching for work and the family stretching its food budget, the question is immediate: how soon will improvement arrive? That question now sits at the centre of Tinubu’s re-election argument. The APC unveiled its second-term manifesto today, defending the administration’s reforms while promising improvements in security, living standards, infrastructure and governance. The campaign is asking Nigerians to connect the disruption of the present with the prospect of a more prosperous future. It is a politically demanding request. Voters must decide whether the government has established a credible foundation for improvement and whether their experience gives them sufficient reason to renew its mandate. A New Manifesto Meets An Existing Record An incumbent’s manifesto arrives with a companion document: the record of the government seeking another term. The APC’s new commitments include additional electricity meters, wider health insurance coverage and a reduction in the number of out-of-school children. Its presentation also promised identifiable delivery responsibilities and public reporting of progress. These are campaign commitments, whose implementation remains to be demonstrated. That creates an opportunity for a more useful election debate. On electricity, candidates should explain how proposed investments would improve supply to homes and businesses. On employment, they should distinguish training places, temporary opportunities and sustained paid work. On education, they should explain how children will enter school, remain there and learn. The opposition has a responsibility here too. Criticism of government performance becomes more persuasive when accompanied by a workable alternative. A promise to make life affordable needs an explanation of costs, funding and consequences. A promise to improve security needs an account of personnel, intelligence, accountability and protection for affected communities. The campaign can now be judged against specific proposals. Nigerians should expect the candidates to defend them. item.title: Tinubu seeks Reps’ approval for $7.7bn external borrowing plan in 2026 budget
item.description: By GiftChapiOdekina, Abuja President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has written to the House of Representatives, seeking legislative approval for the implementation of the N10.79 trillion ($7.7 billion) external borrowing component of the 2026 Appropriation Act. The request, contained in a letter addressed to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, seeks approval to raise $7.707 billion at the budget exchange rate of N1,400 to the dollar to finance part of the Federal Government’s budget deficit. However, the President clarified that the request does not constitute a fresh borrowing plan, explaining that the National Assembly had already approved the amount and made provision for it in the 2026 Appropriation Act. According to him, the current request is aimed at fulfilling the statutory requirements of Sections 21(1) and 27(1) of the Debt Management Office (DMO) Establishment Act, 2003, which require parliamentary approval of the terms and conditions governing external loans. Tinubu explained that Section 21(1) prohibits the Minister of Finance from obtaining or approving external loans unless their terms and conditions have been presented to and approved by the National Assembly. He added that Section 27(1) empowers the National Assembly to approve standard terms and conditions for negotiating and accepting external loans and issuing guarantees. The President recalled that the 2026 Appropriation Act provided for N29.218 trillion in new borrowings to finance the budget deficit, comprising N18.28 trillion in domestic borrowing and N10.79 trillion in external borrowing. He said the Federal Government would pursue multiple financing options simultaneously, taking into consideration their costs, benefits and the time required to access the funds. Tinubu, however, indicated that greater emphasis would be placed on Eurobond issuance, which he said could be concluded more quickly and provide access to larger amounts of financing at relatively lower costs. On the proposed Eurobond issuance, the President noted that the final terms and conditions would be determined at the time of pricing, depending on prevailing market conditions. He assured that the Federal Ministry of Finance and the Debt Management Office would work to secure the most favourable terms available in the international market. According to the letter, the external borrowing is intended to finance projects and programmes captured in the 2026 budget, particularly in priority sectors including defence and security, transportation, agriculture, power, education and health. Tinubu said the borrowing would also support the administration’s efforts to stabilise and strengthen ongoing macroeconomic reforms. He further argued that the proceeds would contribute to the country’s external reserves, as the funds would be received by the Central Bank of Nigeria on behalf of the Federal Government, thereby supporting the naira exchange rate. item.title: Otti urges lawyers to defend rights of vulnerable Nigerians
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, has urged legal practitioners across the country to prioritise access to justice by extending legal services to indigent and vulnerable citizens who cannot afford legal representation. Otti made the call in Umuahia while declaring open the 2026 Nigerian Bar Association Section on Public Interest and Development Law (NBA-SPIDEL) Annual Conference, with the theme, “In Public Interest: Advancing Justice, Democracy and Development.” The governor urged lawyers to adopt a more humane approach to cases involving indigent and vulnerable citizens, stressing that the pursuit of justice should take precedence over professional interests and financial considerations. He said the legal profession had a responsibility to provide assistance to people who lacked the financial capacity to defend their rights. “And because you are lawyers, we need to go the extra mile of asking ourselves, beyond all the things that have been said, how can we be of service to people who cannot pay? “How can we be of service to the vulnerable? How can we help people who on their own cannot afford to help themselves? “Until government gets to that level, we have not cracked the surface. If it is only about you and then the money you make and all that, then you don’t need to be here. You may as well go and do something else,” he said. Otti said his administration had discovered cases of people who remained in correctional facilities despite allegedly having committed no offences warranting their continued detention. He cited the case of an individual who was allegedly detained for supporting an opposition political party, adding that the experience prompted him to direct the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice to work with the Chief Judge to secure the release of such inmates. The governor also warned against the misuse of the justice system to punish citizens for expressing their opinions or engaging in activities on social media, insisting that the protection of individual rights must remain central to governance. On judicial infrastructure, Otti disclosed that his administration would soon commission 10 newly constructed courthouses equipped with renewable energy systems, digitalised court records and broadband connectivity. He also urged lawyers to embrace technological advancements and prepare for emerging changes in legal practice. In his keynote address, former Vice President, Prof. Yemi Osinbajo, urged lawyers to move beyond litigation and legal interpretation to champion public interest, protect disadvantaged citizens and ensure that democracy delivers tangible benefits to the people. Osinbajo identified expensive legal services, prolonged court proceedings, judicial corruption and impunity as major obstacles to access to justice. item.title: Many terrorists neutralised as military sustains pressure on enclaves
item.description: Scores of terrorists have been neutralised across different communities in the Northern region of the country following the pressure sustained in their enclaves by the troops of the Nigerian military. The troops, in different operations sustained pressure on the criminals and dismantled criminal networks with a view to protecting lives and property, and restoring lasting peace and security across the country. Daily Trust reports that the development was in line with the commitment of the Armed Forces of Nigeria under the leadership of General Olufemi Olatunbosun Oluyede. The four-star general, has at different fora maintained that he would continue to ensure that all law-abiding Nigerians, particularly those in the Northern Nigeria sleep with their two eyes closed. Updating Nigerians on the efforts being made to restore peace across the country, the Director, Defence Media Operations, Major-General Michael Onoja disclosed that consistent efforts were made to deny terrorists, kidnappers, gunrunners and other criminal groups’ freedom of action between October 30th and November 5th, 2026. Terrorists suffer heavy losses in Northeast Checks showed that in the North East geopolitical zone, troops of Operation HADIN KAI inflicted heavy losses on terrorists who attempted to strike at troops’ locations in Borno and Yobe States. Subsequently, troops pressed home the advantage with clearance operations and a wave of arrests. On the night of October 29th, 2026, terrorists approached Buni Yadi in Gujba LGA of Yobe State, from the Timbuktu Triangle axis. However, troops countered the attack and subsequent exploitation on 30 October 30th, 2026 discovered the bodies of 48 terrorists, along with 42 AK-47 rifles, five PKT machine guns, four general-purpose machine guns, a 60mm mortar, 105 magazines and two video cameras. The following day, troops’ operations around Apama and Jauro Bashir along the terrorists’ withdrawal route, recovered three corpses, an AK-47 rifle and 188 rounds of ammunition. The senior military officer confirmed that on the same day, terrorists also attempted to infiltrate a troops’ location at Bitta in Gwoza LGA of Borno State but were forced to retreat. He added, “Exploitation at first light recovered the bodies of seven terrorists, four AK-47 rifles, an RPG tube, four RPG bombs, three RPG chargers, a PKM machine gun and a radio. “Troops also received several surrendered members of terrorist groups, rescued escapees and dismantled terrorist support networks across the theatre. “Between 2 – 4 November 2026, twelve terrorist fighters and family members surrendered at New Abaram Resettlement Village and Banki Junction in Bama LGA and near Ngurusoye in Gwoza LGA in Borno State.” On November 2nd, 2026, troops rescued a female abductee who had escaped from the Mandara Mountains at Hudugum, Hambagda, along the Gwoza-Limankara Road.
